newsitem.title: MEXICO: Jalisco to halt corn imports during harvest.
newsitem.headline: Jalisco to halt corn imports during harvest.

text.p: Industrialists in the Mexican state of Jalisco have reached an agreement with corn and sorghum producers to cancel grain imports during the state's harvest from October to February, a federal Agriculture Ministry official said Friday.

"The industrialists who import grains agreed ... to cancel the imports they had filled for the end of the year," Jorge Martinez, a federal Agriculture Ministry delegate to the state of Jalisco, told Reuters in an interview.
"They are not going to fill any grain import spots because there is enough. Grain imports cannot be justified right now," he said.

Jalisco is the top corn-producing state in Mexico with production estimated at 2.34 million tonnes of corn for the harvest that begins this October and ends in February next year. The sorghum harvest is estimated at 561,375 tonnes.
